description: A tech lead must approve the production rate-limiting and query-safety policy for a public GraphQL API, including tenant limits, failure behavior, rollback triggers, and security controls, after the normal cross-functional readiness review.

shared_context.S1: The public GraphQL API is scheduled to move from pilot traffic to general production traffic on Monday.
shared_context.S2: Riley makes the binding decision on the production API policy.
shared_context.S3: The current draft allows 300 requests per minute with a burst of 30 requests, permits schema introspection, allows query depth 12, and has no tenant-specific rate tier.
shared_context.S4: The API readiness review follows a fixed round in which platform, SRE, security, and customer success each state their concrete settings and required follow-up before Riley can finalize the policy.

PF1.text: While profiling traffic for an unrelated dashboard this afternoon, Mei found that the enterprise traffic pattern requires a general enterprise tier of exactly 600 requests per minute with a burst of exactly 120 requests; she has not updated the policy draft yet.

PF2.text: During a resilience rehearsal this morning, Owen confirmed that the limiter currently fails open when its Redis dependency is unavailable; the production policy must fail closed and trigger rollback when denied requests exceed exactly 2 percent for exactly 10 consecutive minutes, but he has not filed the rehearsal result.

PF3.text: While reviewing a security scan for another service, Fatima confirmed that production GraphQL introspection exposes the full schema and that depth 12 permits an expensive nested-query pattern; the API must disable introspection, set maximum query depth to exactly 8, and add a WAF query-depth rule, but she has not opened a security finding.

PF4.text: Lucas confirmed with Atlas Health's account team this morning that its integration contract requires a dedicated limit of exactly 1000 requests per minute with a burst of exactly 60 requests; the contract detail has not yet been added to the API readiness ticket.

acceptance_conditions: The enterprise tier must allow exactly 600 requests per minute.
The enterprise tier must allow exactly 120 burst requests.
The limiter must fail closed when Redis is unavailable.
Rollback must trigger above exactly 2 percent denied requests.
The rollback threshold must apply for exactly 10 consecutive minutes.
GraphQL introspection must be disabled in production.
Maximum GraphQL query depth must be exactly 8.
Atlas Health must receive exactly 1000 requests per minute with a burst of exactly 60 requests.
The settlement must require a WAF query-depth rule.
The settlement must require an Atlas Health-specific rate-tier commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The draft's 300-per-minute and 30-burst defaults change to exactly 600 requests per minute and exactly 120 burst requests for the enterprise tier.
The limiter behavior changes from the draft's unspecified dependency failure handling to fail-closed operation with rollback above exactly 2 percent denied requests for exactly 10 minutes.
The production security settings change from enabled introspection and depth 12 to disabled introspection, exactly depth 8, and a required WAF query-depth rule.
Atlas Health's contract changes its tenant settings to exactly 1000 requests per minute and exactly 60 burst requests and requires an Atlas-specific rate-tier commitment.
